v.why: Raising an already large Adam learning rate destabilizes training (e.g. exp 7 lost 9 to 35 points on all three datasets).
Backing off from a very large learning rate recovers accuracy (exps 12, 14, 18, 19 all gained).
With a tiny learning rate, 243 epochs underfit, so a larger step helps (exps 1, 2, 10).
Lowering an already tiny learning rate worsens underfitting.
Deeper nets are less stable at high learning rates (exp 47 lost 4 to 39 points).
Shallower nets tolerate high learning rates better (exps 53, 57, 60 mostly gained).
Strong L2 regularization underfits, so reducing it helps (exps 91, 99, 92).
Pushing an already strong L2 penalty higher increases underfitting.
Very small batches give noisy updates, so a larger batch stabilizes training (exps 24, 27, 30).
Larger batches reduce gradient noise, which offsets the instability of a high learning rate (exps 27, 30, 23).
